tasks.short: Check regulatory work against green initiatives.

steps.what: List the green initiatives the company has already adopted.
Monitor regulatory activities against those green initiatives.
Record alignment or the gap the manager found.

tasks.design: Adopted green initiatives are listed from {DOCS}. The regulatory affairs manager monitors each regulatory activity against those initiatives and records alignment or a gap. An initiative that is not adopted is not on the list. The screen does not declare the activity green.
tasks.previous_blocker: Green goals sat in a strategy slide, and regulatory files were not read against them.
tasks.enabler_now: An initiative the company has adopted can be a checklist item.
tasks.still_hard: A goal that is a slogan rather than a rule, and an activity the list does not describe.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can see an activity that meets the letter and misses the initiative.
tasks.altitude: The adopted rules are listed. Alignment is still the manager's judgement. Nothing is marked green by the screen.

reach.task: Compare an activity to an adopted goal and record the gap.
reach.learn: The list can be shared. The alignment judgement stays here.

evidence.claim: A register can list initiatives the company has adopted. It cannot judge alignment.
Calling an activity aligned is the manager's record. An initiative that is not adopted is not used as a rule. No automated green label is applied.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Initiative id and activity id, produced by the initiative register. An activity with no initiative list is not marked aligned. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the initiative list the company has already adopted.
unknowns: Which initiatives are adopted rather than proposed.
Who owns the green label outside regulatory affairs.
research_questions: Which initiatives have a written rule?
What share of regulatory files were never checked against them?

already_counted.description: The manager still records the gap.

incremental.description: The manager adds an initiative when it is adopted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the list of adopted initiatives. It disappears when the initiatives are not written down and the manager reads the strategy slide. The judgement remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate discoveries and depositions with legal.

steps.what: Index the documents legal staff asked for.
Coordinate discoveries and depositions with legal staff.
Note what was handed to the legal department.

tasks.design: Documents named in the legal request are indexed from {DOCS}. The regulatory affairs manager coordinates discoveries and depositions with legal staff. The index does not mark a document privileged and does not decide relevance. The note lists only what the manager handed over.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived by mail and the same file was hunted twice, once for a deposition and once for a discovery.
tasks.enabler_now: A named document can be indexed once the legal request lists it.
tasks.still_hard: Privilege, relevance, and a document the request describes but does not name.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell legal that a named file is the wrong version.
tasks.altitude: The index is a list of named files. Coordination stays with the manager and legal staff. Privilege is not marked by the screen.

reach.task: Index papers counsel named and leave privilege to counsel.
reach.learn: The index can be mechanical. The handover conversation cannot.

evidence.claim: An index can list documents a request names. It cannot decide privilege or relevance.
Privilege is a legal judgement. The screen must not mark it. The manager coordinates; legal staff decide what is privileged.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Request id and document id, produced by the legal request. A request that names no document id produces an empty index. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the document store the company already keeps. Do not add a privilege field.
unknowns: Which matters are under a hold.
research_questions: Are discovery requests specific enough to name document ids?
What must never be copied into the index?

already_counted.description: The manager still coordinates with legal.
The manager still writes the handover note.

incremental.description: The manager corrects an index line that pointed at the wrong version.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the index of documents the request already names. It disappears when the request is descriptive and the manager searches. The coordination time is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch emerging industry rules for process impact.

steps.what: Filter emerging trends in industry regulations.
Summarise each trend and the process it might affect.

loop.input: one industry item and the process list
loop.check: the summary names only a process on the list
loop.stop: stop when every item is summarised or rejected
loop.why_not_simpler: industry commentary is prose, and a keyword rule misses a renamed process

steps.what: Decide the potential impact on organisational processes.

tasks.design: A filtered feed in {DOCS} shows industry items from sources the manager named. A summary may name only a process already listed. The regulatory affairs manager decides the potential impact, including no impact. The feed does not change a process. An item with no decision stays open.
tasks.previous_blocker: Industry commentary was forwarded in mail and died there, so a real change arrived late.
tasks.enabler_now: Named sources can be filtered and each item can wait for a decision.
tasks.still_hard: A source the filter misses, and a summary that sounds more certain than the item.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell a vendor essay from a rule that will change a process.

ambition.what: Each industry item on the named feed is marked impact or no impact in the week it appears.

tasks.altitude: The queue is current. The impact decision stays with the manager. No process is changed by the summary.

reach.task: Queue an external item and record whether it changes a named process.
reach.learn: The queue is the same pattern. The process impact is decided here.

evidence.claim: A filtered feed can queue an industry item and a summary can name a process already listed. The owner decides the impact.
The job digest's rule watch stops when every item has a decision. A summary may not name a process that is not on the list. No process is edited by the feed.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Source id, item id, and process id, produced by the source list and the process register. An unknown source is not summarised. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use sources the manager has already named.
unknowns: Which industry sources are in scope.
How the manager wants no-impact items retained.
research_questions: What share of items were noise last quarter?

already_counted.description: The manager still decides the impact.

incremental.description: The manager rejects a summary that named a process not on the list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the filter and the summary. It shrinks when a source is wrong and the manager reads the items. The impact decision remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare the brief on the proposed environmental policy.
Meet environmental regulatory agencies about the proposed policy.
Write the potential impact learned in the meeting.

tasks.design: A brief on the proposed environmental policy is taken from {DOCS} before the meeting. The regulatory affairs manager meets the state or federal agency and writes the potential impact. The brief is not sent as the company's position. No relationship is recorded as agreement unless the manager writes it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proposed environmental rules were read alone, and the agency's informal view was lost.
tasks.enabler_now: The proposed text can be one brief. The meeting is unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: An agency view that is not yet a rule, and a relationship that depends on the person in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can hear a direction the proposed text does not state.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays with the manager. The brief is only the papers. No impact is inferred by the screen.

reach.task: Meet an environmental authority and write what was indicated.
reach.learn: The brief can be prepared. The relationship cannot be a feed.

evidence.claim: A brief can collect a proposed text. It cannot develop a relationship with an agency.
What an agency indicates in a meeting is the manager's note. The screen must not convert a proposal into an impact.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.
Fields: Proposal id and document id, produced by the policy file. A meeting with no document still happens. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the files already stored for that proposal.
unknowns: Which agencies this company actually meets.
Whether state or national bodies lead.
research_questions: Which proposals are active enough to brief?
What may be written down after an informal meeting?

already_counted.description: The manager still meets the agency.
The manager still writes the impact.

incremental.description: The manager adds a paper the brief missed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the brief. It disappears when the proposal is new and the manager builds the pack for the meeting. The meeting time is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A green rule and an industry item can be queued. The manager still judges alignment, still sits with legal on discoveries, and still meets the environmental agency.
reach: Chief sustainability officers compare an activity to a stated green rule and record the gap.
Compliance managers index papers for counsel and do not mark privilege themselves.
skills_to_grow: Record alignment against a green rule the company has already adopted, and stop when the rule is missing.
Index a document for legal staff without marking it privileged.
role.ambitious_version: An industry rule on the feed is marked for impact or no impact in the week it appears, and the agency relationship stays a meeting.
